stem.en: How does the diversity of organisms help keep an ecosystem balanced and stable?

text.en: Plants, pollinators and decomposers each do a job that others depend on.

feedback.en: Right. Plants make food, animals pollinate and disperse seeds, and microorganisms recycle nutrients.

text.en: With more species, each one needs less food, so nothing ever runs short.

feedback.en: Species do not need less food in a rich forest. They depend on one another.

text.en: Diversity stops storms, disease and pollution from ever reaching a forest.

feedback.en: Diversity can lower some risks. It cannot stop them from reaching a forest.

text.en: Only the largest animals matter, and rich forests hold more of these.

feedback.en: Each species, large or small, plays an important role.

explanation.en: Each species plays a role. Plants produce food and oxygen, animals pollinate flowers and disperse seeds, and microorganisms recycle nutrients. When one species goes, others that depend on it may decline.

hints.en: Think of what the tree, the bee and the fungus each do for the others.
